questions.stem: Elements in the modern Periodic Table are arranged in order of increasing:
questions.explanation: The modern Periodic Table arranges elements by increasing atomic number (number of protons). Mendeleev originally arranged elements by atomic mass, but this led to some elements being in the wrong group. The arrangement by atomic number correctly places all elements according to their properties.

questions.stem: Element X is in Group 1 and Period 3 of the Periodic Table. What is its electronic structure?
questions.explanation: The period number tells you the number of electron shells (3 shells), and the group number tells you the number of electrons in the outer shell (1 electron). With 3 shells and 1 in the outer shell, the electronic structure is 2, 8, 1. This is sodium (Na). Option (a) would be Period 2, Group 1 (lithium).

questions.stem: Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table. Why was this considered a strength of his work rather than a weakness?

options.text: The gaps made the table easier to read
He predicted undiscovered elements and their properties, which were later confirmed
The gaps allowed him to fit more elements into the table
Other scientists filled the gaps with their own elements

questions.explanation: Mendeleev predicted the existence and properties of undiscovered elements (like gallium and germanium) based on the patterns in his table. When these elements were later discovered and matched his predictions closely, it provided strong evidence that his periodic table was fundamentally correct.

questions.stem: What do elements in the same period of the Periodic Table have in common?

options.text: The same number of electrons in their outer shell
The same number of electron shells

questions.explanation: Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells. For example, all Period 3 elements have 3 electron shells. Elements in the same group (not period) share the same number of outer shell electrons and have similar chemical properties.

questions.stem: An element has 2 electrons in its first shell, 8 in its second shell, and 6 in its third shell. Where is this element found in the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: This element has 3 electron shells, placing it in Period 3. It has 6 electrons in its outermost shell, placing it in Group 6. With 16 electrons total (2 + 8 + 6), this is sulfur (S). The period number always matches the number of occupied electron shells, and the group number matches the number of outer electrons.
